subject: Learning Methods
title: Interference Theory
description: A quick, practical guide to Interference Theory.

hook.text: You learned French in school. Then Spanish. Now when you try French, Spanish words keep intruding.

buildup.text: Interference theory says forgetting happens because similar memories compete with each other.

discovery.text: Proactive interference: old memories block new ones. Retroactive: new memories overwrite old ones.

twist.text: The more similar two sets of information are, the more they interfere. Distinct material suffers less.

climax.text: Vary your study subjects. Studying two similar topics back to back maximizes harmful interference.

punchline.text: Similar memories fight. Space them apart.

quiz.question: What is retroactive interference?
options: Old memories prevent new ones from forming
New memories disrupt or overwrite old ones
Memories fade due to lack of sleep
